text:
maria: Quick design review — playground streaming UI. Need quick takes on: 1) Stop vs Regenerate placement (inline vs separate), 2) Token counter during stream (visible / collapsed / hidden), 3) Prompt library access pattern (panel vs flyout). Mock in Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/xyz — TL;DR: leaning inline stop + compact token badge. Thoughts? alex: Inline stop + regen next to it on hover feels least disruptive. Primary action during streaming should be Stop. :thumbsup: cheng: Accessibility note: Stop must be keyboard reachable and announced. Use an `aria-live` region for partial streaming updates and ensure the stop button has a visible focus ring. Example: ```
``` `aria-pressed` isn’t right for Stop since it’s not a toggle. jordan: Token counter — keep it visible as a small badge (top-right of message area) but collapse digits while chars are streaming to avoid layout shift. Show exact token count on hover. Also call out cost tooltip: we should surface an estimated token cost while streaming. samira: Prompt library: don't force a modal. Prefer a right-side flyout or drawer (`Ctrl+K` to open). Keyboard interactions: focus should move into the library and pressing `Esc` closes it and restores focus to composer. Also ensure screen-reader label on each saved prompt. :white_check_mark: alex: Copy nit: consider renaming `Stop` → `Interrupt` to make it clear we can resume/regenerate. But `Stop` is shorter. Open to debate. maria: Good points. UX question for eng: when user hits Stop mid-stream, should Regenerate reuse KV/cache so regen is faster? Also should Stop emit an analytics event `stream_interrupted` with token count so we can monitor? cheng: Runtime note: regen can reuse KV only if the same model+context and the underlying request path is identical. If prompt or system messages changed, we do a cold start. We can expose a boolean `warm_cache:true` in the response metadata so the UI can show a toast: "Using warm cache — faster response". jordan: Keyboard nav: put Stop in the tab order immediately after the last message or composer. Example screen-reader hint on stop: `role=button` + `aria-describedby` pointing to a small hint: "Stops current generation; use Regenerate to try again." Also use `role=alert` on stream end to announce completion. samira: Accessibility checklist I'll add to the Figma comments: focus order, aria-labels, contrast for token badge, keyboard shortcuts, screen reader text for prompt library items. I’ll add a11y test cases. maria: Implementation notes for product copy: if we go with `Interrupt` we should update hover tooltip to: "Interrupt generation (partial result preserved)." If we stick with `Stop` tooltip: "Stop generation (partial output retained)." Which do folks prefer? alex: Leaning `Interrupt` + shorter tooltip. cheng: Either fine. Make sure telemetry event differentiates user-initiated stop vs error stop. ui-bot: Reminder: design sync on this landed PR scheduled for Fri 2026-03-27 — prototype with token-badge collapsed state and flyout prompt library needed before sync. maria: Thanks all — I'll update the mock and rename states accordingly. If anyone has strong objections to `Interrupt` vs `Stop`, drop a :thinking_face: in this thread by EOD tomorrow.
